result_revision.change_summary: Initial dev result for the released CarBench checkpoint.

methodology.record_note: Released CarBench checkpoint (carbench-weights-v1.0, transolver_large.pth) run unchanged; every native surface point of all 1,154 official_test designs is predicted directly. Training compute is a labelled estimate reconstructed from checkpoint timestamps.

architecture.description: Large Transolver variant with dropout 0.1, predicting surface pressure from per-point coordinates and outward normals.

components.description: Large Transolver variant with dropout 0.1, predicting surface pressure from per-point coordinates and outward normals.

input_features.name: surface_coordinates
input_features.description: Native surface-point x/y/z in metres, normalized with training-set statistics.

input_features.name: surface_normals
input_features.description: Consistently auto-oriented VTK point normals of the native surface.

predicted_fields.description: Kinematic gauge pressure (m^2/s^2) at every native surface point, denormalized with training-set mean and standard deviation.

data_handling.normalization: Pressure standardized with training-split mean -94.5 and standard deviation 117.25 m^2/s^2; predictions are de-standardized before writing.
data_handling.preprocessing: Native surface read unchanged; no remeshing. Point normals from VTK compute_normals with consistency and auto-orientation.
data_handling.sampling: Training: one fixed 10,000-point random subsample of native surface points per design, preprocessed once and cached. Inference: ceil(N/10000) disjoint seeded random 10,000-point passes cover every native point once; the final pass is padded with already-predicted points for context and only new points are kept.

stages.description: Supervised training on the official DrivAerNet++ training split with model selection on the official validation split.

loss.description: Mean-squared error on standardized pressure at the sampled surface points.

duration.description: 244 epochs run; the released checkpoint is the lowest validation-loss epoch (244).

compute.measurement_notes: Reconstructed from the run's checkpoint timestamps (results/transolver_large, 2025-10-25): 71 s per epoch; the released best checkpoint (epoch 244) was written 5.1 h after start. Training continued for early-stopping patience after that, so total wall time was somewhat longer. Single run with PyTorch DataParallel (multi_gpu enabled) on a 4 x A100-SXM4-80GB machine; the visible device count was not recorded and is assumed to be all four.

checkpoints.bytes_description: Raw bytes of transolver_large.pth from the CarBench v1.0 weights release, loaded unchanged.
checkpoints.role: Exact loaded checkpoint for every prediction.
checkpoints.selection_rule: Lowest official-validation loss, selected before any test-case inference.

inference_compute.hardware: 1 x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB shared with other inference processes
inference_compute.measurement_notes: Wall time from first to last prediction file. Ran concurrently with up to nine other inference processes across two GPUs. Includes VTK reading, preprocessing, all passes and serialization; excludes model loading and the FluidsBench evaluator.

note: Dev result for a released CarBench checkpoint; not owner-approved and not an official result.

evaluation.command: python scripts/drivaernetplusplus.py evaluate-entry transolver_large-entry --output work/transolver_large --resume && python scripts/drivaernetplusplus.py package --evaluation-root work/transolver_large/evaluation --config package-config-transolver_large.json --discretization-cases discretization-cases.jsonl --checkpoint carbench-transolver-large=transolver_large.pth --output submissions/drivaernetplusplus/drivaernetplusplus-carbench-transolver-large-dev-v1
